headline: AI cuts Korean herbal medicine prep time from 300 minutes to 5 by automating manufacturing, not diagnosis.
summary: Korean startup Onerve uses AI to standardize and automate herbal medicine production, reducing prep time significantly. The system handles manufacturing, cleaning, and packaging, leaving complex diagnosis to human doctors.
details: Korean startup Onerve, backed by the Korea Institute of Oriental Medicine, has developed the HAP system to automate Korean herbal medicine manufacturing. This AI-powered system connects with electronic medical records, drastically cutting prep time for a single dose from 300 minutes to just 5. Onerve won a CES Innovation Award and secured a Series A funding round of approximately 6.2 billion won.

The key insight behind HAP's success is its strategic application of AI: it automates the repeatable manufacturing process, not the nuanced diagnostic and prescribing judgment of Korean medicine doctors. This division ensures that human expertise remains central to patient care, while machines handle standardized production.

A critical innovation was standardizing raw materials. Traditionally messy and inconsistent herbs are now processed into uniform, freeze-dried "cartridge" formats. This standardization of inputs was the true bottleneck, enabling the machine to take over the precise production steps.

Beyond speed, the system delivers crucial consistency. Traditional methods can lead to batch-to-batch variations in concentration and cooking. The standardized cartridge format ensures predictable and reproducible potency for every dose, a vital factor in medical applications where reliability is paramount.

Onerve is not alone in this emerging field; another Korean company, Camelotech, also presented a similar automation system at CES. This indicates that "Korean herbal medicine automation" is becoming a recognized and growing category within the industry.

headline_marked: [[Cloudflare launches AI wallets]] for agents with infrastructure-enforced spending caps
headline: Cloudflare launches AI wallets for agents with infrastructure-enforced spending caps
summary: Cloudflare's new system allows AI agents to spend money via virtual wallets, but with crucial spending limits enforced at the infrastructure level. This design aims to prevent prompt injection attacks and ensure secure autonomous transactions.
details: Cloudflare has launched "Cloudflare Wallets" and cloudflare.pay, a new system designed for AI agents to manage spending. The core idea involves an Account Wallet for humans and Virtual Wallets with limited spending power granted to individual AI agents via API keys. This is a directional statement, with full funding and programmatic controls coming in "the next few months."

The system functions like a company's master account issuing prepaid cards to AI "employees," where spending limits are hard-coded into Cloudflare's infrastructure. Payments leverage the x402 protocol, enabling agents to pay for services on the spot with stablecoins.

This move aligns with a broader industry trend, following Coinbase's x402 protocol in May 2025, Google's AP2 in September 2025, and Mastercard's Agent Pay in April 2025. These separate initiatives highlight a collective industry push towards building infrastructure for an "agent economy" projected to reach $3-5 trillion by 2030.

The critical innovation is the spending cap enforced by the platform itself, not the AI agent's internal logic. This infrastructure-level enforcement is designed to block prompt injection attacks at the payment layer, meaning an agent cannot exceed its allocated budget even if compromised.

Placing the spending cap at the infrastructure layer is crucial because agents can be "talked out of" their own internal rules by malicious prompts. An external, unalterable limit ensures true security, preventing an agent from overriding its budget regardless of its instructions.
